subject.title: [Bug] Telegram exec approval bubble not dismissed after clicking approve

question: Should maintainers close or ignore the open fork PR and queue a fresh target-repo fix for the active Telegram approval runtime?
rationale: The bug shape is clear, but an open fork PR still uses closing syntax for this issue and targets an obsolete handler path, so automation should not create another fix PR until maintainers decide how to handle that candidate.

options.title: Queue a fresh narrow fix
options.body: Close or explicitly ignore the fork PR, then fix `extensions/telegram/src/approval-handler.runtime.ts` with the shared delete final-action seam and real Telegram proof.

options.title: Adopt the fork manually
options.body: Manually port only the useful idea from the fork into the active runtime path, dropping obsolete handler and unrelated docs changes.

options.title: Wait for fork refresh
options.body: Keep this issue blocked on the fork author rebasing and retargeting the patch, accepting that the issue remains unresolved in main and the latest release.

recommendation.title: Queue a fresh narrow fix
recommendation.body: Close or explicitly ignore the fork PR, then fix `extensions/telegram/src/approval-handler.runtime.ts` with the shared delete final-action seam and real Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The native approval lifecycle refactor introduced the active owner boundary that the fix should use.
